exclude.motion.hover-state/micro-lift: Cards that lift on hover are a listed giveaway, and lift plus tinted shadow is the kit default. Only 13 to 18% of CTAs use a transform at all, and tone-step or fill rows cover this slot better.
exclude.motion.load-sequence/film-opening: Needs a real rendered film or object, and holds the page for 4 to 6s. A model's version is a cheap imitation in front of the content.
exclude.motion.load-sequence/percent-counter: Needs real assets to load. A generated page has nothing to load, so the count becomes a fake timer, and load.md already says not to show one then.
exclude.motion.scroll-pin-or-scrub/camera-flight: Needs real 3D scenes and a page with no conversion job. A model's scenes end up as procedural objects at poster scale.
exclude.motion.scroll-pin-or-scrub/wheel-gated-s: Takes the wheel away from the reader, and its own spec says expressive sites only. Expressive hands skip flags, so it stays available there.
exclude.motion.scroll-reveal/rise-stagger-row: A rise and fade on entry is the fade-up on every block. A model dealt this row spreads it down the page, and only 3 of 66 measured reveal rows are this form.
exclude.section.logo-wall/press-masthead-row: An 'as seen in' row needs real coverage and real mastheads. On an invented business it is a made-up claim set in letterforms a model cannot draw.
exclude.section.pricing-table/flip-board-price: A split-flap prop is named as a costume in anti-patterns: a gimmick doing the job of design, on the section that most needs to read plainly.
exclude.section.stats/rating-row: Invented scores from named platforms. This is the five-star tell from 6 of 16 GPT runs, plus a false source.
exclude.section.team/candid-group-photo: Real people in a real place cannot be generated. The whole form depends on an asset a model cannot produce.
exclude.section.testimonial/press-quotes: Invented quotes and scores attributed to real outlets are fabricated proof, and the form depends on publisher marks a model does not have.
exclude.section.testimonial/video-testimonials: Depends on real footage of real customers. A play ring over a generated still is reliably cheap.

motion.hover-state/arrow-nudge.reason: Fine on one link, but dealing it invites an arrow on every button, and arrows bolted on are a listed giveaway (16 of 16 GPT runs).

motion.hover-state/scale-pop.reason: Scale 1.05 on hover is the kit default. Only 13 to 18% of CTAs use any transform, and most change fill.

motion.load-sequence/colour-plate-mark.reason: A splash before the page. Fine for a hotel, but preloaders are only 5 to 6% of SaaS and devtool load rows, and load theatre is a measured Opus tell.

motion.load-sequence/headline-word-cycle.reason: The rotating word is a template move, and it stacks on the marked-word giveaway. Only worth it when the audiences are real.

motion.load-sequence/iris-or-sheet-revea.reason: A covered entrance of 1 to 1.5s whose shape must come from the brand, and a model invents the shape. Reads as load theatre.

motion.load-sequence/mark-performs.reason: Needs an owned mark, which a freshly invented brand lacks, and holds a flat screen for 1.5 to 3s.

motion.load-sequence/staged-fade-stair.reason: A real Linear-style move, but readable only by about 1.9s and easy to overrun. Models already keep heroes changing past 0.3s.

motion.load-sequence/title-card-hold.reason: Holds a blank card and 110px type for about 2.5s before the page. Load theatre plus an oversized headline.

motion.load-sequence/typed-title.reason: The typewriter headline is the cheap version of this idea, and it delays the first readable sentence.

motion.load-sequence/word-blur-resolve.reason: Headline is not readable until well past 1s. Past the 1.2s limit in load.md for a selling page, and blur reveals are overused.

motion.load-sequence/wordmark-docks-to-n.reason: Covers the page for about 2s and locks scroll. Good when chosen for a brand, wrong as a default on a page with a job to do.

motion.scroll-pin-or-scrub/sticky-card-d.reason: Translucent cards with 22px blur land on the glass-cards giveaway, and stacked full-screen statements invite one sentence per screen.

motion.scroll-reveal/blur-front-wipe.reason: Same scrubbed-reading failure as word-ink-scrub, with a gradient band and blurred text on top.

motion.scroll-reveal/word-ink-scrub.reason: Scrubbed reading is a measured Opus tell: most paused frames show a half-lit sentence. Real on gold sites, but only as a deliberate showpiece.

section.case-study/brand-poster-tiles.reason: Needs custom art per customer. The spec warns a bare gradient reads as missing, and a gradient is what a model will reach for.

section.cta-band/character-or-joke-close.reason: Needs a real mascot a model cannot draw well, or a joke that lands in the Opus deadpan tic.

section.cta-band/floating-object-ring.reason: Scattered tiles around a heading echo the orbiting logo ring from GPT runs, and the objects must be real, which an invented brand lacks.

section.cta-band/giant-type-sign-off.reason: 100 to 250px display type with an accent last word hits two giveaways: the oversized headline and the marked word.

section.cta-band/inset-colour-panel.reason: The tinted CTA band of the template stack, and the commonest close. Loud bands are 24% of all closes but 10% of gold.

section.feature-sticky-scroll/scrubbed-s.reason: Pinned type as the event: scrubbed reading plus one sentence per screen, both measured Opus tells.

section.footer/ghost-wordmark-crop.reason: Pale ghost wordmarks are named in anti-patterns from a reject and an Opus footer, and models reach for them to add weight cheaply.

section.footer/giant-wordmark-finish.reason: Real on gold beside a true index, but 7 of 16 Opus runs already end this way. Fine when chosen, overused by default.

section.footer/object-signoff.reason: Tilted paper labels and stickers are the hero-sticker habit moved to the footer. Its own spec limits it to personal sites and strong concepts.

section.integrations/orbit-and-arc.reason: Logos orbiting a tile appeared in 3 of 3 GPT PM runs, and the chapter names it as the cheap version.

section.logo-wall/masked-grey-marquee.reason: The default 'trusted by' strip, the commonest row in the family, though only 31% of walls move. With invented logos it is the template at its most visible.

section.testimonial/drifting-double-row.reason: The infinite moving cards pattern from component kits. It needs about thirty public quotes, and a model fills it with stock names.

section.testimonial/portrait-story-cards.reason: The photo must show the real person. Without real portraits the form collapses into generated faces under a scrim.
